# dsytri2x

> Computes the inverse of a real symmetric indefinite matrix using the factorization produced by `dsytrf` (classic Bunch-Kaufman, worker routine called by `dsytri2`).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsytri2x from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsytri2x';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsytri2x( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, IPIV, strideIPIV, WORK, nb ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'`, must match the factorization |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix `A` |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix (factored form from `dsytrf`) |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in | `N` |  | pivot indices from `dsytrf` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IPIV` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `N + nb + 1 × nb + 3` |  | workspace of length `(N+nb+1)*(nb+3)` |
| `nb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | block size |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the details of the factorization are stored as an upper or lower triangular matrix.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular, form is $A = U \, D \, U^T$;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular, form is $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the NNB diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L as computed by DSYTRF.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the (symmetric) inverse of the original matrix. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the upper triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A below the diagonal is not referenced; if `UPLO = 'L'` the lower triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A above the diagonal is not referenced.
- `IPIV`: Details of the interchanges and the NNB structure of D as determined by DSYTRF.
- `nb`: Block size

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success; `> 0` = the `(k,k)` element of `D` is exactly zero so the inverse cannot be computed)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsytri2x.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    nb
) → integer
```

Computes the inverse of a real symmetric indefinite matrix using the factorization produced by `dsytrf` (classic Bunch-Kaufman, worker routine called by `dsytri2`), using alternative indexing semantics.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'`, must match the factorization |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix `A` |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix (factored form from `dsytrf`) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `A` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in | `N` |  | pivot indices from `dsytrf` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IPIV` |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `IPIV` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `N + nb + 1 × nb + 3` |  | workspace of length `(N+nb+1)*(nb+3)` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |
| `nb` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | block size |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the details of the factorization are stored as an upper or lower triangular matrix.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular, form is $A = U \, D \, U^T$;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular, form is $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the NNB diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L as computed by DSYTRF.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the (symmetric) inverse of the original matrix. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the upper triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A below the diagonal is not referenced; if `UPLO = 'L'` the lower triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A above the diagonal is not referenced.
- `IPIV`: Details of the interchanges and the NNB structure of D as determined by DSYTRF.
- `nb`: Block size

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success; `> 0` = the `(k,k)` element of `D` is exactly zero so the inverse cannot be computed)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, $D(i,i) = 0$; the matrix is singular and its inverse could not be computed.

</section>

-   `dsytri2x()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DSYTRI2X`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dsytri2x.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dsytri2x from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsytri2x';

// Trivial 1x1 example: the factored form of [[5]] is itself, and its inverse is [[0.2]].
const A = new Float64Array( [ 5.0 ] );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( [ 0 ] );
const work = new Float64Array( 20 );

const info = dsytri2x( 'column-major', 'lower', 1, A, 1, IPIV, 1, work, 2 );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSYTRI2X`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSYTRI2X computes the inverse of a real symmetric indefinite matrix A using the factorization $A = U \, D \, U^T$ or $A = L \, D \, L^T$ computed by DSYTRF.

</section>
